Alison —

Appreciate the clear asks. I've sketched initial recommendations and attached a spreadsheet (voltcloud-scaling-proposal.xlsx) with conservative and aggressive bands. High-level answers below; see the spreadsheet for per-model and per-sequence-length breakdowns.

SUMMARY RECOMMENDATION (pilot, single tenant private pool, us-west-2):
- Sustained target: 1.2k qps (approx 30k tokens/sec assuming 25 tokens/request avg) with p50 ~ 60ms token-add and p95 ~ 180ms under normal load.
- Peak/burst target (short windows): 4k qps absorbed for up to 10 minutes if the warm-pool is fully primed; otherwise fallback to a smaller, lower-cost model variant.
- Buffer commitment: recommend a committed slab sized for sustained + 20% headroom (i.e., commit to 1.5k qps equivalent). Warm pool/auto-burst should cover the rest.
- Egress: plan for ~22 Gbps per 8-GPU slab when fully saturated with embeddings-heavy workloads; typical generation traffic will be closer to 4–8 Gbps per slab depending on sequence length and KV-cache hit rate. Cross-AZ: recommend keeping inference in one AZ per customer for latency and egress predictability; if VoltCloud requires active-active AZs we will provision separate pools and replicate models (adds ~10–12% overhead).

Runbook highlights:
- Warmup: pre-warm KV caches for the top 50 request prefixes during campaign windows (script included in spreadsheet).
- Cache-warm paths: use prefix caching and small aggregator layer to reduce cold-start token costs. Expect 20–40% latency improvement for primed caches.
- Fallbacks: automatic downgrade path to a 4-bit quantized variant + shorter seq cap at 512 tokens; model-variant fallback is immediate, with a degrade-notify webhook to VoltCloud ops.

I've looped in Karthik, Grace, and Dylan to validate the sizing math and network assumptions. If that matches your procurement timeline we'll push a PO-ready one-pager and a priced commitment table by Friday EOD.

Best,
Rachel Kim

Rachel / team —

Quick math and assumptions (details in attached CSV: privpool-sizing-math.csv):
- Assumptions: avg tokens/request = 25; model latency per token (baseline) = 60ms p50 with optimized kernels; KV cache hit rate 55% for pilot traffic; 8xA100-80GB slab peak throughput ~ 4.8k qps for short sequences (seq <= 512) when fully saturated.

Sizing table (rounded):
- Sustained 1.2k qps -> requires 1 x 8-GPU slab (util ~25%) for latency headroom and scheduling. We recommend 2 slabs committed (provides sustained + 25% absorb and maintenance window capacity).
- Committed slab recommendation: 2 x 8-GPU slabs (commit) + 1 warm slab for short lived bursts (autoscale to 4k qps observed via warm pool). Warm slab can be shared for short bursts if isolation constraints permit.
- Burst absorption: with warm slab and KV priming, we can absorb up to 4k qps for ~10 minutes before throttling or fallback; beyond that we recommend immediate fallback to quantized variant.

Network/egress:
- 8-GPU slab saturated with generation-heavy traffic (~200 tokens/req average) would approach 40 Gbps; conservative planning for mixed traffic: 8 Gbps (gen-light) -> 22 Gbps (emb-heavy). Recommend requesting 25 Gbps per slab as a procurement line item for headroom and cross-AZ replication safety.
- Cross-AZ: strong recommendation to avoid cross-AZ inference due to unpredictable network egress and increased p95s. If VoltCloud requires active-active across AZs, double the committed slabs and add ~12% egress overhead per additional AZ.

Runbook notes:
- Warmup script: run prefix warm for top 50 prefixes 30 minutes before campaign start.
- Cache validation: daily KV-hit-rate report and automated priming if hit-rate drops below 40%.
- Fallback policy: immediate model variant swap + circuit-breaker to ingestion pathway; notify VoltCloud via webhook and page Redwood infra.

I'll attach the CSV with per-model per-seq calculations. If Grace/Dylan agree on operational constraints I'll give Rachel a short bulleted commit table to send back to VoltCloud.

-karthik
